mainTopic: The ערבה ceremony around the מזבח: the משנה, the place מוצא, the willows standing on the יסוד, and the פסוק 'אסרו חג בעבותים'
overview: This amud opens by finishing the previous discussion. The גמרא rejects the reading that the לולבים were put 'on the roof', and corrects it to 'on the bench' (איצטבא). רב יהודה adds that the הר הבית had a double colonnade, so there was room for everyone's לולב. A new משנה then describes the ערבה ceremony in the מקדש. Willows from מוצא were stood around the מזבח, the שופר was blown, and the people circled the מזבח once each day and seven times on the seventh day, saying הושיעה נא. The משנה also explains how the ceremony worked on שבת, gives רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view about beating palm branches, and says that children then ate their אתרוגים. The גמרא explains that מוצא was a קלניא exempt from the king's tax. From the willows' height of 11 אמות, מרימר proves that they stood on the יסוד of the מזבח. רבי אבהו gives the פסוק 'אסרו חג בעבותים', and quotes רבי אלעזר that taking a bound לולב and a thick-leaved הדס is like building a מזבח and bringing a קרבן. The פסוק for that teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why would anyone want to dry out the לולבים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges a reading that the לולבים were put on the roof, because that would dry them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does he need to dry them out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the לולבים brought to the הר הבית on ערב שבת were placed on a roof. A roof in the sun would dry them out, and nobody wants that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the text said the attendants arranged the לולבים 'on the roof'. The גמרא points out that a לולב must stay fresh to remain כשר and beautiful. Putting it in the sun on a roof makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so that…? (a rhetorical challenge opener)

phrases.english: And does he need to dry them out?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. Obviously he does not want dry לולבים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous amud about where the לולבים brought to the הר הבית on שבת were placed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the לולבים were placed on the roof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A roof would dry out the לולבים, and drying them is the opposite of what is wanted.

steps.title: Correct the text: on the bench
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording to 'on the bench' (איצטבא) instead of the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the text. The לולבים were placed on a bench, not on the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אלא אימא' means the earlier wording is replaced. An איצטבא is a covered bench area beneath the roof. There the לולבים stay shaded and fresh.

keyTerms.meaning: bench, a raised seating area under a covered porch

phrases.english: Rather, say:
On top of the bench.
phrases.notes: A shaded spot, so the לולבים do not dry out.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לולבים were laid on the roof.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were laid on the shaded bench, where they stay fresh.

steps.title: The Temple Mount had a double colonnade
steps.stepSummary: רחבא in the name of רב יהודה says the הר הבית had a colonnade inside a colonnade.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבא said in the name of רב יהודה: The הר הבית was a double colonnade, one colonnade inside another.
steps.whatsHappening: רחבא quotes רב יהודה to describe the layout of the הר הבית. It was surrounded by two rows of covered porches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains how a bench area could hold the לולבים of the whole crowd. Two covered colonnades gave plenty of shaded room. It supports the corrected reading of step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: colonnade, a covered porch with pillars

phrases.english: Rachava said in the name of (Rav) Yehuda:
The Temple Mount was a double colonnade,
a colonnade inside a colonnade.
phrases.notes: So there was enough covered bench space for everyone's לולב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies background facts that make the 'bench' reading workable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הר הבית had two layers of covered colonnades.
steps.whatToRemember: The לולבים on שבת were stored in the shade on the benches of the double colonnade, not on the roof.

steps.title: משנה: gathering willows from מוצא and standing them by the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה describes where the ערבות came from and how they were set up around the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How was the מצות ערבה done? There was a place below ירושלים called מוצא. They would go down there and gather tall willow branches. Then they would come and stand them upright at the sides of the מזבח, with their tops bent over the top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains the ערבה ceremony in the מקדש, starting with gathering the willows and placing them around the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is different from the ערבה in the ארבעה מינים bundle. Here, large willow branches decorated and surrounded the מזבח itself. The branches were tall enough that their tops leaned over onto the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of the willow in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This ערבה is not the ערבה inside your לולב bundle. It is a separate מקדש ceremony with big branches standing around the מזבח.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How is the מצוה of the willow done?
There was a place below Jerusalem
and it was called "Motza."
They would go down there
and gather from there tall willow branches,
and come and stand them upright at the sides of the altar,
and their tops were bent over the top of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the לולב discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Willows from מוצא were stood around the מזבח with their tops leaning over it.

steps.title: Shofar blasts, daily circling, and the prayer said
steps.stepSummary: They blew תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה, circled the מזבח once a day, and said 'אנא ה' הושיעה נא'. רבי יהודה gives a different wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: They blew a תקיעה, a תרועה, and a תקיעה. Every day they circled the מזבח once and said: 'Please, ה', save us; please, ה', grant success.' רבי יהודה says they said: 'אני והו, please save us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the ceremony. It describes the שופר blasts, the daily walk around the מזבח, and the words said during it, with רבי יהודה disagreeing about the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא quotes the פסוק in תהלים directly, using the name of ה'. רבי יהודה says they used the special phrase 'אני והו' instead of saying the name directly. This is the source of our הושענות on סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: they blew a long blast, a broken blast, and a long blast
a special phrase substituting for the Divine name

steps.whyThisMatters: These circlings are the root of our הושענות, and the seven circlings of the seventh day are the root of הושענא רבה.

phrases.english: They blew a tekia, a terua, and a tekia.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ פַּעַם אַחַת
phrases.english: Each day they circle the altar one time
and say:
"Please, Lord, save us,
please, Lord, grant us success."
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in תהלים 118:25.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"Ani vaho, please save us."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ceremony after the willows are set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They circled the מזבח once daily, saying הושיעה נא. רבי יהודה disputes the exact words.

steps.title: Seven circlings on the seventh day and the farewell words
steps.stepSummary: On the seventh day they circled seven times. At departure they praised the מזבח, and רבי אלעזר gives another version.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day they circled the מזבח seven times. When they left, what did they say? 'Beauty to you, O מזבח! Beauty to you, O מזבח!' רבי אלעזר says: 'To ה' and to you, O מזבח; to ה' and to you, O מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the special seventh day, when they circled seven times. It also gives the farewell words said to the מזבח when they finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'That day' means the seventh day of סוכות, our הושענא רבה. The תנא קמא's farewell praises only the מזבח. רבי אלעזר adds ה' first, so the praise is clearly directed to ה׳ together with the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: and on that day (the seventh day of סוכות)
at the time of their departure

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים.
phrases.english: And on that day they circle the altar seven times.
At the time of their departure, what do they say?
"Beauty to you, altar! Beauty to you, altar!"
Rabbi Elazar says:
"To the Lord and to you, altar; to the Lord and to you, altar."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the seventh day with the regular days of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven circlings on the seventh day; farewell praise to the מזבח, with רבי אלעזר adding ה'.

steps.title: The ערבה ceremony on שבת
steps.stepSummary: On שבת the ceremony was the same, but the willows were gathered the day before and kept fresh in gold basins.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is done on a weekday, so it is done on שבת. The only difference is that they gathered the willows on ערב שבת and placed them in golden basins so they would not wilt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens when the ערבה day falls on שבת. The ceremony itself is unchanged; only the gathering is moved earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking willows at מוצא on שבת would be forbidden, so they were picked on Friday. To keep them fresh overnight, they were stood in water in golden basins. The ceremony itself pushes aside שבת, but the preparation does not.

phrases.english: As its performance on a weekday, so is its performance on Shabbat,
except that they would gather them from the eve (of Shabbat)
and place them in basins of gold,
so that they would not wilt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ceremony to the special case of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבה ceremony takes place on שבת, but the willows are gathered on ערב שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: beating palm branches
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says they brought palm branches and beat them on the ground by the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: They would bring palm branches and beat them on the ground at the sides of the מזבח, and that day was called 'the day of beating palm branches'.
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא gives his own description of the seventh-day ceremony. In his version, palm branches were brought and beaten on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה describes a seventh-day ritual using palm branches; the משנה itself does not say whether this replaced the willows or was done in addition to them. He reports that this was famous enough to give the day a name, חבוט חריות.

keyTerms.meaning: the beating of palm branches (name of the day)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
They would bring palm branches,
and beat them on the ground at the sides of the altar,
and that day was called "the beating of palm branches."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different view of the seventh-day ritual from the one described in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the seventh day, palm branches were beaten on the ground beside the מזבח.

steps.title: Children take apart their לולבים and eat their אתרוגים
steps.stepSummary: Right after the seventh day's מצוה, children would take apart their לולבים and eat their אתרוגים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, the children take apart their לולבים and eat their אתרוגים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by describing what children did once the מצוה of the ארבעה מינים was finished on the seventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the last day of taking the לולב was over, the מינים were no longer needed for the מצוה. The children would then undo the bundle and eat the אתרוג, as an expression of joy.

phrases.english: Immediately, children pull apart their lulavim
and eat their etrogim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה with what happens after the seventh-day מצוה is complete.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the seventh day's מצוה, the מינים may be taken apart and the אתרוג eaten.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה describes the ערבה ceremony: willows from מוצא around the מזבח, daily circling and הושיעה נא, seven circlings on the seventh day, and the same ceremony on שבת with the willows picked the day before.

steps.title: A ברייתא: מוצא was a military colony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא saying that the place מוצא was a קלניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: It was a קלניא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that gives a different description of the place the משנה calls מוצא. This sets up the next question about the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא identifies the place as a קלניא, a Roman colony. That raises a question: if this is what it was, why did our משנה call it מוצא? The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmudic discussion on the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught: It was a place of a colonia (military colony).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה by clarifying the place name מוצא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The place called מוצא was a קלניא.

steps.title: Why does our משנה call it מוצא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our תנא calls the place מוצא if the ברייתא calls it a קלניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, why does he call it מוצא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the name our משנה uses for the place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources use different names for the same place. The גמרא wants to know what the name מוצא means and why our משנה chose it.

keyTerms.meaning: and our תנא (the author of our משנה)

phrases.english: And our tanna, what is the reason
that he calls it "Motza"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא דִּידַן מַאי טַעְמָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ מוֹצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the gap between the ברייתא's name and our משנה's name.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name מוצא and why our תנא uses it.

steps.title: Because it was released from the king's tax
steps.stepSummary: It is called מוצא, meaning 'taken out', because it was exempt from the royal tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it was released from the king's tax, it is called מוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name מוצא means 'taken out', because the place was taken out of the king's tax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two names do not conflict. As a Roman colony (קלניא), the place was exempt from the royal tax. מוצא, meaning 'removed' or 'let out', describes that same exemption.

phrases.english: Since it is released from the king's tax —
he calls it "Motza" (taken out).

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוצא means 'released', since the colony was exempt from the king's tax. So both names describe the same place.
steps.whatToRemember: מוצא and קלניא are the same place. The name מוצא reflects its exemption from the royal tax.

steps.title: The willows were 11 cubits tall and leaned over the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about standing the ערבות at the sides of the מזבח. A ברייתא then adds that they were many, long, and 11 אמות high, so they would bend one אמה over the top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'They came and stood them up at the sides of the מזבח.' A ברייתא taught: the willows were many and long, and 11 אמות high, so that they would lean over the מזבח by one אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and adds details from a ברייתא about how tall the ערבות were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the ערבות were stood up by the מזבח. The ברייתא adds a key number: 11 אמות tall, so that the top bends one אמה over the מזבח. That number is what the next step will use to work out exactly where the ערבות were placed.

phrases.english: And they come and stand them upright at the sides, etc.
phrases.notes: This is just quoting the משנה to show which part we're about to discuss.

phrases.english: It was taught: numerous, and long,
and eleven cubits high,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ גּוֹחוֹת עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אַמָּה.
phrases.english: so that they would lean over the altar one cubit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after the discussion of the place called מוצא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבות were 11 אמות tall and leaned one אמה over the מזבח

steps.title: מרימר infers that the willows stood on the יסוד of the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: מרימר, quoting מר זוטרא, learns from the ברייתא that the ערבות were placed on the יסוד, the base of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר said in the name of מר זוטרא: Learn from this that they placed the willows on the base of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר states a conclusion that he draws from the ברייתא: the ערבות stood on the יסוד. The next step will explain how he knows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never says where the bottom of the ערבות rested. מרימר claims the numbers only work if the ערבות stood on the יסוד, which is one אמה off the ground. This is an inference, and the proof comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, conclude from this
The base of the מזבח, its first one-אמה step

phrases.english: Mareimar said in the name of Mar Zutra:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עַל הַיְּסוֹד מַנַּח לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Learn from it that one places them on the base,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עַל הַיְּסוֹד מַנַּח לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical conclusion from the ברייתא's measurement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבות were placed on the יסוד, not on the ground

steps.title: The altar's measurements show the ground would not work
steps.stepSummary: The proof: if the ערבות stood on the ground, the מזבח's height and its step-ins would make it impossible for an 11-אמה willow to lean one אמה over the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think they placed them on the ground, there is a problem. The מזבח went up one אמה and stepped in one אמה; that is the יסוד. It went up five more and stepped in one אמה; that is the סובב. It went up three more; that is the place of the קרנות. So how could the willows lean over the top of the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves מרימר's point by describing the shape of the מזבח and showing the willows could not reach over it from the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח is about nine אמות tall, and it gets narrower as it rises, so a willow on the ground must lean at an angle to reach the top. At that angle, 11 אמות is not long enough to also bend one full אמה over the top. Standing it on the יסוד gives it an extra אמה of height, and the numbers work.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, if you would think
The ledge that surrounds the middle of the מזבח
The 'horns,' the raised corners at the top of the מזבח
How can you find it? How could this happen?

steps.confusionAlert: עלה means 'went up' (height), and כנס means 'stepped inward' (the מזבח gets narrower). Both kinds of numbers matter: the step-ins are what force the willow to lean at an angle.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אַאַרְעָא מַנַּח לְהוּ, מִכְּדֵי:
phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that one places them on the ground, now since:

phrases.aramaic: עָלָה אַמָּה וְכָנַס אַמָּה — זֶהוּ יְסוֹד.
phrases.english: It ascended a cubit and indented a cubit; that is the base.

phrases.aramaic: עָלָה חָמֵשׁ וְכָנַס אַמָּה — זֶהוּ סוֹבֵב.
phrases.english: It ascended five and indented a cubit; that is the surrounding ledge.
It ascended three; that is the place of the horns.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹחוֹת עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ!
phrases.english: Leaning over the top of the altar, how can you find it?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: it would be impossible

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אַאַרְעָא מַנַּח לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for מרימר's inference
steps.raayaObject: That the ערבות stood on the יסוד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The known measurements of the מזבח compared with the 11-אמה height in the ברייתא

steps.title: Conclusion: the willows stood on the base
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ערבות must have been placed on the יסוד and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that they placed them on the יסוד? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof and agrees that the ערבות were placed on the יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since standing on the ground fails the math, the only option left is the יסוד. The closing 'שמע מינה' shows the גמרא fully accepts מרימר's inference.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that...? (leads to the only remaining option)

steps.whatToRemember: The ערבות were 11 אמות tall and stood on the יסוד of the מזבח, so they could bend one אמה over its top.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַיְּסוֹד מַנַּח לְהוּ.
phrases.english: Rather, is it not that we learn from it that one places them on the base?
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof begun in step 15
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ערבות were stood on the יסוד of the מזבח

steps.title: The verse behind the willows around the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives the פסוק that hints to the ערבות surrounding the מזבח up to its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What is the source in the פסוק? As it says: 'Bind the festival offering with thick branches, up to the horns of the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו brings a פסוק from תהלים as the source for placing ערבות around the מזבח so that they reach its top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עד קרנות המזבח' (up to the horns of the מזבח) match the idea that the ערבות reached up and leaned over the top. 'בעבותים' is read as leafy branches surrounding the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asks for a scriptural source)
Bind the festival (offering), from תהלים קיח:כז

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: What is the verse?
As it is stated: 'Bind the festival with branches'
'until the horns of the altar.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a scriptural source for the practice just clarified
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'אסרו חג בעבותים עד קרנות המזבח' is the source for the ערבות surrounding the מזבח

steps.title: Taking a proper lulav and myrtle is like bringing an offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes רבי אלעזר: whoever takes a bound לולב and a thick-leaved הדס is treated by the פסוק as if he built a מזבח and brought a קרבן. The פסוק that proves it comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי אלעזר: Anyone who takes a לולב tied together and a הדס with thick leaves, the פסוק counts it for him as if he built a מזבח and brought a קרבן on it, as it says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that reads the same פסוק a different way. It ends with 'as it says,' setting up the פסוק that will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'אסרו' is read as binding the לולב, and 'עבותים' as the thick-leaved הדס. Because the פסוק continues 'until the horns of the מזבח,' doing the מצוה properly is compared to building a מזבח and offering a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Its binding, the לולב tied together
Its thick, leafy form (a kosher הדס)
The פסוק credits him, counts it for him

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the details of a מצוה, like binding the לולב and using a full הדס, add great value, comparing the מצוה to the עבודה of the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who takes a lulav in its binding
and a myrtle in its dense-leaved form,
the verse credits him

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ בָּנָה מִזְבֵּחַ וְהִקְרִיב עָלָיו קׇרְבָּן,
phrases.english: as though he built an altar and offered a sacrifice on it,
as it is stated:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is quoted at the start of the next passage

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק to teach a new lesson about לולב and הדס
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking a bound לולב and a thick-leaved הדס is counted as if one built a מזבח and offered a קרבן
